You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 26 [20 marks]: How can financial strategies affect the objectives of financial management?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of how financial strategies affect objectives of financial management | Applies relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a sustained, logical and cohesive response and communicates clearly using relevant business terminology and concepts
13–16 marks: Demonstrates a sound understanding of how financial strategies affect objectives of financial management | Uses relevant case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Presents a logical and cohesive response using relevant business terminology and concepts
9–12 marks: Demonstrates some understanding of how financial strategies affect objectives of financial management | Makes reference to case study/studies and contemporary business issues | Communicates using business terminology and concepts
5–8 marks: Describes some aspects of financial strategies and/or financial objectives | Makes limited reference to case study/studies and/or contemporary business issues | Communicates using some business terminology and/or concepts
1–4 marks: Makes limited reference to financial strategies and/or financial objectives | May identify case study/studies | Uses basic business terminology and/or concepts


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Objectives of financial management:
• Profitability, growth, efficiency, liquidity, solvency
• Short term and long term.
Financial management strategies:
• Cash flow management
– cash flow statements
– distribution of payments, discounts for early payment, factoring
• Working capital management
– control of current assets – cash, receivables, inventories
– control of current liabilities – payables, loans, overdrafts
– strategies – leasing, sale and lease back
• Profitability management
– cost controls – fixed and variable, cost centres, expense minimisation
– revenue controls – marketing objectives


WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: identify financial strategies and financial objectives from the syllabus
Better responses: make detailed links between how each strategy was able to achieve a financial objective
Better responses: apply case studies to show specifically how a business was able to use the strategy
Better responses: show comprehensive knowledge by linking a strategy to multiple objectives. For example, factoring improves liquidity but in the long term reduces profitability; or expense minimisation improves profitability, and this allows the business to achieve growth in the future
Better responses: use appropriate business terminology throughout.
To improve: referring to financial strategies from the syllabus, not strategies from other topics or general tasks of a business
To improve: implementing case study knowledge and applying it to each strategy
To improve: understanding the key term of 'how' requires the student to explain a connection between the strategy and the objective
To improve: writing in detail and providing a sustained response.

STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-20>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '17–20'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a 6 to 8 line plan of what a full-mark response would cover, one line per paragraph, not a full essay>"}
